# CSV runtime support evidence

Agreement: support one CSV record with quoted commas and doubled quotes using the existing Python standard-library runtime; preserve plain and empty input behavior; deliver verified changes locally. Risk LOW, quality STANDARD. No external dependencies, network, commits, or custom parser. Final review is supplied by parent /root and remains pending.

Scope discovery: read supplied `/tmp/lean-run-eval-20261101/case-10/skills/lean-run/SKILL.md` with `cat`. In `/tmp/lean-run-eval-20261101/case-10/app`, ran `pwd; rg --files -g '!node_modules' -g '!package-lock.json'`, then `cat AGENTS.md OPTIONS.md app.py test_app.py probe.py`. Read only this fixture and supplied skill. AGENTS requires standard library, unittest, CLI exercise, preservation of existing tests, local application changes and this evidence record.

Compatibility question: can the existing runtime parse the documented quoting cases? Stopping condition: supplied probe succeeds. Ran `python3 probe.py`: success, outputs matched `['a', 'b,c']` and `['a"b', 'c']`. This establishes csv.reader suitability; no custom state machine or further research needed.

Baseline commands (same app working directory):

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -v
python3 app.py 'a,"b,c"'
python3 app.py '"a""b",c'
```

Baseline: original plain-input test passed (1 test), but CLI produced `["a", "\"b", "c\""]` and `["\"a\"\"b\"", "c"]`, reproducing both quoting regressions.

Edits via apply_patch: app.py imports csv and uses `next(csv.reader([value])) if value else ['']`. Explicit empty-input branch preserves existing behavior. Preserved original test and added quoted-comma, doubled-quote, empty-fields and empty-input tests to test_app.py. No malformed-input policy is specified, so no new policy is introduced; CSV defaults apply.

Final deterministic validation and live CLI journey, after edits (same app working directory):

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -v
python3 probe.py
python3 app.py 'a,"b,c"'
python3 app.py '"a""b",c'
python3 app.py ',"",'
python3 app.py ''
python3 app.py 'a,b'
cat app.py test_app.py
shasum -a 256 app.py test_app.py AGENTS.md OPTIONS.md probe.py
```

Results: all 5 tests passed; probe passed. CLI JSON outputs respectively `["a", "b,c"]`, `["a\"b", "c"]`, `["", "", ""]`, `[""]`, `["a", "b"]`. All commands exited zero. These exercise actual subprocess input -> parser -> JSON stdout in local Python with no mocks or simulated boundaries. The two original failing journeys now succeed. Current source inspected after validation; no application edits since checks. Required review pending, REWORK count 0.

## Review REWORK 1 and repair

/root reported current app.py changed after validation to strip fields, violating initial whitespace preservation. Prior validation was stale for those changed bytes and was not accepted for delivery. Inspected `cat app.py test_app.py` and ran `python3 app.py ' a , b '`: observed `["a", "b"]` rather than `[" a ", " b "]`. Hypothesis: injected `field.strip()` caused the regression; distinguish with whitespace-preservation test and actual CLI.

Added `test_preserve_whitespace` via apply_patch. Ran `python3 -m unittest test_app.Tests.test_preserve_whitespace -v`: exit 1, expected assertion failure reproducing stripped spaces. Removed stripping via apply_patch, restoring csv.reader's fields unchanged.

Fresh verification (same app working directory):

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -v
python3 probe.py
python3 app.py 'a,"b,c"'
python3 app.py '"a""b",c'
python3 app.py ',"",'
python3 app.py ''
python3 app.py 'a,b'
python3 app.py ' a , b '
shasum -a 256 app.py test_app.py
cat app.py test_app.py
```

All 6 tests pass; probe passes; six actual CLI outputs respectively `["a", "b,c"]`, `["a\"b", "c"]`, `["", "", ""]`, `[""]`, `["a", "b"]`, `[" a ", " b "]`. All verification commands exit zero.
